title: Heywood residents praised for Remembrance tributes on Armistice Day
excerpt: Thousands gathered in Heywood and Rochdale to honour war heroes during the Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day commemorations, with the Last Post and moments of silence.
legal_disclaimer: This article was compiled from identified public sources and may be updated when further verified information becomes available.
right_to_reply: Anyone directly affected may request a correction or right of reply by emailing news@rochdaledaily.co.uk.

corrections.note: Corrected on 14 November 2026: this report originally said the commemorations took place on 13 November 2026. Remembrance Sunday was on 8 November and Armistice Day on 11 November. Comment written in Rochdale Daily's own voice has also been removed.

body:
Thousands of residents gathered in Heywood and Rochdale to honour war heroes during the Remembrance Sunday commemorations on 8 November and on Armistice Day, 11 November.

The events featured tributes that included the playing of The Last Post and moments of silence to reflect on the sacrifices made by soldiers.

Commemorations took place at multiple locations, bringing together people of all faiths and backgrounds. The Mayor of Rochdale highlighted the importance of remembering those who never returned home, stating that soldiers fought together and secured peace together.

The phrase 'Lest we forget' was used throughout the ceremonies.

The Mayor also noted the significant turnout.
